<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="מנחם אב_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919939_theRebbe_869" batchId="meluket-_D7_9E_D7_A0_D7_97_D7_9D_20_D7_90_D7_91_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919939_theRebbe_869__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the connection between the encompassing level of Chayah and the internal levels of Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah is achieved through the service of self-sacrifice (mesirut nefesh) stemming from the level of Yechidah, which unifies all faculties in fulfilling G-d's will.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And likewise is it in the service of man,</t>
    <t s="1">that in order for there to be a connection of the aspect of Chayah</t>
    <t s="2">(encompassing)</t>
    <t s="3">with the aspect of Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah</t>
    <t s="4">(internal),</t>
    <t s="5">so that the love of "with all your soul" will be felt also in the internal powers</t>
    <t s="6">[and likewise the connection of the intellect and the emotions],</t>
    <t s="7">it is through the service of mesirut nefesh (self-sacrifice),</t>
    <t s="8">which is from the aspect of Yechidah.</t>
    <t s="9">And one can explain from the elucidations on this,</t>
    <t s="10">that by one giving himself over to G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="11">the essence of all his powers is to fulfill the will of the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="12">And since the encompassing and the internal</t>
    <t s="13">[and likewise the intellect and the emotions]</t>
    <t s="14">their essence is not their own existence but rather to fulfill the will of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="15">therefore they do not contradict each other, and on the contrary, they become joined together.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the enactment to recite one hundred blessings daily was specifically when one hundred people died each day, because the revelation of the power of self-sacrifice comes through concealments, and the one hundred blessings unite the encompassing and filling aspects through the letter Alef of "one hundred."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is that the enactment to recite one hundred blessings each day was specifically when one hundred souls died each day,</t>
    <t s="2">because the revelation of the power of mesirut nefesh is through concealments and veils.</t>
    <t s="3">[And according to the known principle</t>
    <t s="4">that in the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="5">and particularly in the generation of the footsteps of Moshiach,</t>
    <t s="6">the power of mesirut nefesh is more revealed than in the time of the Holy Temple].</t>
    <t s="7">And therefore,</t>
    <t s="8">the enactment to recite one hundred blessings was specifically after one hundred souls died each day,</t>
    <t s="9">because this that each day one hundred souls died</t>
    <t s="10">(for one hundred souls is the completeness of number)</t>
    <t s="11">is because they were then in a state opposite to freedom from the Angel of Death,</t>
    <t s="12">which is the evil inclination,</t>
    <t s="13">and through this the power of their mesirut nefesh was then aroused.</t>
    <t s="14">And therefore they enacted then to recite one hundred blessings,</t>
    <t s="15">through which is made the connection of the Surrounding and the Filling,</t>
    <t s="16">because through the revelation</t>
    <t s="17">(of the power of mesirut nefesh that is from)</t>
    <t s="18">the Yechidah, there is a drawing down of Atik,</t>
    <t s="19">the Alef of "one hundred,"</t>
    <t s="20">the aspect of "one and not in number,"</t>
    <t s="21">and through this is made the connection of "Mah"</t>
    <t s="22">(Filling)</t>
    <t s="23">and "Me'ah"</t>
    <t s="24">(Surrounding),</t>
    <t s="25">read not "Mah" but "Me'ah."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the Midrash that "Now" implies repentance, and that the verse "Now Israel, what does G-d ask of you" refers to one hundred blessings, because the revelation of self-sacrifice is primarily through repentance, enabling the service of one hundred blessings.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, we can also explain the statement of the Midrash</t>
    <t s="1">"There is no 'Now' except the language of repentance, as it is said, 'Now Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you.'"</t>
    <t s="2">And according to the known principle</t>
    <t s="3">that all the interpretations of that verse are connected to each other,</t>
    <t s="4">it is understood</t>
    <t s="5">that this that "Hashem your G-d asks of you 'Mah'"</t>
    <t s="6">— one hundred blessings —</t>
    <t s="7">is related to the matter of repentance,</t>
    <t s="8">and "Now."</t>
    <t s="9">For since penitents conquer their inclination more than the completely righteous,</t>
    <t s="10">and in order for a person to be able to stand against his inclination, it is through remembering the matter of mesirut nefesh,</t>
    <t s="11">therefore,</t>
    <t s="12">the primary revelation of the power of mesirut nefesh is in penitents.</t>
    <t s="13">And this is "Now etc., 'What does Hashem your G-d ask of you,'"</t>
    <t s="14">for through the revelation of mesirut nefesh that comes through repentance,</t>
    <t s="15">"Now,"</t>
    <t s="16">it is possible to have the matter of one hundred blessings,</t>
    <t s="17">"What does Hashem your G-d ask of you."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
